newsitem.title: USA: N.J. details proposed $3.4 bln taxable bond deal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. details proposed $3.4 bln taxable bond deal.

text.p: Gov Christine Whitman's administration proposed Monday to borrow $3.4 billion to invest in the New Jersey pension funds it operates for public employees.
State officials said the bond issue would enable the administration to eliminate about $623 million it now contributes to the fund from the state budget.
Gov. Whitman, who is seeking re-election this year, is scheduled to introduce her fiscal 1998 budget on Jan. 29.
Treasurer Brian Clymer said the bonds would not be tax-exempt.

The financial maneuver is an attempt to capitalize on the strong performance of the pension fund's investment portfolio. Its return has averaged 12.4 percent since recovering from the 1981-82 recession, while the borrowing would cost no more than 8.75 percent, state officials said.

The Whitman administration had reduced the state's annual contribution by nearly $700 million a year in its FY 1994 budget, and actuaries agreed that this would have to be made up starting early in the next century.
Consultants for the public employee unions, which opposed the maneuver, said the estimates relied upon by Clymer were too optimistic about continued performance in the investment portfolio.

The state operates pension funds for 433,300 active workers and 154,500 retirees. These include employees of state, county and local governments and the public schools. They contribute between five and seven percent of their salary to retirement benefits, varying with seniority.
The proposed bond issue would not affect this schedule.
